summary: Turkish kapatmak is integrated into the existing II paradigm as a lexical verb. Dough, chest and envelope closure remain sense 1, not light-verb collocations.

JTM 2.7/13 adds Infectum-wa: mqapṭiwole has the 3pl finite ending and suffixed dough patient. By contrast mqapṭéwayna in MAC NE interview 1/5 is a plural Part. Pass. with a past copula and clothed state holders; keep it under Detransitive Part. Pass.

The Part. Pass. appears attributively with a bridge, predicatively with doors/gates and clothed people, and substantivized as 'the closed ones' at 64/125. These are distributional functions, not new senses.

Chest closure at 60/38 has an implicit container object and aʕle referring to the enclosed boy. ṭ+l assimilation yields mqapaṭṭe. The coordinated ṣxire w mqapṭe in 96/128 is useful contact evidence without proving a distinct meaning of either conjunct.

Round 2, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations below reproduce the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses and sense distinctions rest on the Turoyo. Round-one proposals are retained as the comparison baseline and are not republished in this JSON.
Round-one Detransitive Part. Pass. already has five examples; the surgical leg and enclosed privy contexts are not added merely because readers counted only one baseline example.

Unprefixed qəpotawo, qəpotaṯṯe and qəpoṭo-yo are action nominals. Their shape and lack of an agent are insufficient to assign Detransitive; file the secure action nouns under Infinitiv II.1 provisionally.
Turkish-derived closure vocabulary has both source t and ṭ spellings and an unprefixed command Qapetu. These source forms are preserved without inventing a separate qpt root or normalising emphasis.
Mqapatwole is Preterit-wa with an l-agent. The machine rendering used to does not justify reclassifying it as Infectum-wa. In mqapaṭle, -le is the l-agent, not by itself proof of an object suffix.
Confirm that mqapṭéwayna in the clothing description is Part. Pass. plus past copula; the plural covered-state reading is used here.
Does the coordination ṣxire w mqapṭe at 96/128 distinguish locking from closing, or reinforce one state? This context alone cannot establish a new numbered sense.
Confirm directive mqapət in Jan 1.8/201 as Infectum versus Imperativ; the published filing is provisional.
Is Qapetu at 154 a reduced integrated II Imperativ or a code-switched loan command? Confirm before reconstructing an Imperativ paradigm.
Do the unprefixed closing nouns belong productively to II, or are they separately borrowed formations? No Detransitive paradigm is inferred.
What is closed at Jan 2.23/4118: the notebook or a named geomantic operation? No technical numbered sense is added.
At Jan 1.46/1997 does mqapto denote sutured closure, contraction, or another leg condition? The already-full state cell is not expanded with this uncertain quotation.
Restore the missing n in dann.
rationale: The supplied JL translation has und dann füllen; dan is a misspelling of the temporal adverb.

summary: The covering/closing state applies to clothed people, gates and doors, alongside the inherited covered bridge; no separate sense is needed.

Closing schools extends the object to institutions; physical closure, administrative shutdown and covering remain within existing sense 1. The geomancy opening/closing pair does not yet establish a distinct technical sense.
